Chapter Five: Facing Corruption and Building a New Home for Children.
Every step forward brought a new set of hurdles. Navigating the child welfare world in Nepal—it was anything but simple. You had poverty shaping every decision, corruption lurking in the shadows, and the scars of war touching everything.
Here’s the tough part—many of the so-called orphanages weren’t what they claimed to be. Some were operated by traffickers, preying on the most vulnerable. Others were run by people with kind hearts but simply overwhelmed by the need. The whole system was stretched thin, and sadly, it was the children who suffered most.
Trying to reunite kids with their families? That was a battle in itself. Local officials would suddenly demand bribes. Important paperwork would just vanish. Promises—gone as quickly as they were made. The frustration was enough to make anyone want to give up.
But it became clear: if real change was going to happen, it would take more than just good intentions. It called for grit, creativity, and the courage to face some pretty uncomfortable truths.
That’s when the decision was made—to create a brand-new home for children rescued from trafficking. The idea was simple: give them safety, stability, and the hope of reuniting with their families. But making it happen? Far from simple. Finding the right building felt impossible at times. Getting funding, hiring staff you could trust—every step was a mountain to climb. The risks were huge, and the obstacles seemed never-ending.
Still, the vision was always there. This new home would be a place to heal, where kids could finally be kids again. The focus was on building a real sense of family—a place where everyone belonged. The team worked day and night to create routines, offer education, provide medical care, and, most importantly, give comfort and support.
And you could actually see the change. Kids who’d arrived guarded and silent started to open up, little by little, learning to trust again.
One evening really stood out. The children were gathered around the dinner table, and something was different. There was laughter, chatter, a feeling of peace. The journey had been so hard, but you could see—these kids were finally thriving. Their hope was coming back.
Of course, the work was nowhere near done. The fight against trafficking pressed on, and the search for families was still ongoing. The challenges—they were still huge. But you couldn’t ignore the progress. It was real.
What started as one person’s journey had grown into something much bigger. Now, it was about the children, their families, the dedicated staff, and everyone who refused to lose hope. It was proof that, even against impossible odds, hope can survive—and lives can be changed.
